prerequisites: High school Mathematics I and II

learning_outcomes.text: Operate and represent real functions of real variables, obtain their limits, determine their continuity, calculate derivatives, and formulate and solve optimization problems.
Handle the concepts of sequences and series and use power series to represent functions.
Formulate and calculate integrals of single-variable functions and apply them to solving engineering-related problems.
State and apply the basic properties of real functions of several real variables. Obtain their limits, analyze continuity and differentiability, and solve optimization problems.

Students must have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students must be able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, enabling the learning of new methods and technologies, as well as providing great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the Telecommunication Technical Engineer's activity.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, task planning, and other similar works in their specific field of telecommunications.

syllabus_topics: Numerical Sets and Functions: Natural numbers, Induction method, Real numbers, Absolute value of a real number and its properties, Elementary functions, Function composition and inverse function.

Limits and continuity: Definition of limit, Properties, Infinitesimals and infinities, Indeterminations, Asymptotes, Continuous functions, Properties of continuous functions (Bolzano's theorem, Darboux's (intermediate value) theorem, and Weierstrass's theorem).

Differentiability. Properties of differentiable functions: Derivative of a function at a point, Derivative function, Differentiability and continuity, Properties of the derivative, Chain rule, Rolle's theorem, Lagrange's mean value theorem, L'Hôpital's rule.
Taylor Polynomial: Successive derivatives, Taylor polynomial, Taylor formula with remainder.
Optimization: Local study of a function, Monotonicity, Relative extrema, Concavity and inflection points, Absolute extrema, Graphical representation of functions.
Calculation of primitives: Immediate integrals, Integration methods.
The definite integral: Basic concepts and geometric interpretation, Integrable functions, Properties of the definite integral, Fundamental theorem of integral calculus, Barrow's rule, Applications.
Improper integrals: Definition of improper integral, Types, Application to the study of Eulerian integrals.
Numerical sequences: Definition, Convergence, Calculation of limits.
Numerical series: Definition, Convergence and sum, Harmonic series and geometric series, Convergence criteria.
Power series. Power series expansion: Definition, Radius of convergence, Differentiation and integration, Power series expansion of a function: Taylor series, Commonly used expansions.
The Euclidean space Rn: Basic notions of topology in Rn, Real functions, Vector functions.
Limits and continuity: Limit of a function at a point and properties, Calculation of limits, Continuity of a function, Properties.
Differentiability: Directional derivative, Partial derivative, Geometric interpretation, Higher-order derivatives, Differentiation and continuity.
Differentiation: Differential of a function at a point, Linear approximation, Sufficient condition for differentiability, Gradient vector, Tangent plane, Chain rule.
Optimization: Free relative extrema, Necessary condition, Sufficient condition, Absolute extrema, Constrained relative extrema, Lagrange multipliers.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, it is mandatory to obtain a minimum of 3.5 points out of 10 in the Theoretical Exam (TE). The final grade is calculated as 0.15 x PL + maximum (0.15 x PA + 0.7 x TE, 0.85 x TE). If the minimums are not reached, the qualification will be failed with a numerical grade equal to TE. In extraordinary calls, a single exam comprises a theoretical part (TE) for which a minimum of 3.5 points is required, and the PA grade is saved from the ordinary period, while PL can be kept or retaken.
